reader_notes: Independent reading from the note text (dump.ts, bars 0-25), under PROTOCOL.md; no published analysis consulted. x = E A C B E B D (seven sixteenths, 1:1.25-1:2.75) landing on C at 1:3: a rising broken chord with a neighbour turn. y = the eighths that follow x in the same voice, C E G# E (1:3-1:4.5); y' = its variant C A G# E (bass 2:1). z = a descending broken-chord figure of seven or eight sixteenths landing on the next beat (first at 3:1.25, E C E A C E G -> F). z mirrors x's direction (falling arpeggio against rising) but is not an exact inversion of it, so it is named separately; read as a free inversion of x it would be x-INV. Notes were searched with small scripts only to confirm alignments; every call below was read in the passage.

opening.leader_meanwhile: free counterpoint: the eighths y (C E G# E) against x in the bass; at 2:1 the leader takes x again (same pitch) while the bass takes y' (C A G# E), so the pair x/y is exchanged at once within bars 1-2 (an exchange reading is also possible; the pilot inven01 calls the same pattern free counterpoint)
opening.notes: Before its entry the bass plays a short continuo line (A2 A3 G#3, 1:1-1:2.5). Bar 2 repeats the pair at the same pitch (x in the right hand at 2:1.25, in the bass at 2:3.25), not on another degree as in inven01. Not a canon: the follower does not copy y.

members.reason: The bass now leads with x on G (6:3.25 G C E D G D F -> E) and the right hand follows two beats later (7:1.25); y' in the bass at 7:1 (E C B G), y in the right hand at 7:3 (E G B G), second x in each voice (bass 7:3.25, right hand 8:1.25). Four x's as in the prime. The leader's line drops a sixth and the follower's rises a tenth: inversion at the double octave. VARY: the prime's continuo notes are replaced by a rest in the right hand (6:3.25-7:1).

Tonic return of the opening: x in the right hand at 18:1.25, then y' (C A G# E); the bass has y' at 18:1 (in place of the continuo notes) and x at 18:3.25, 8 below, 2 beats later. Only the first bar: at 19:1 the arpeggio passage of the close takes over instead of the second pair of x's.

notes: Form call unsure: the PAC in e at 13:3 falls exactly at mid-piece and the second half has a tonic return of alpha at 18, which is rounded bipartite; but the first half is itself two parallel sections (alpha+beta to C, alpha'+beta' to e), and the second section begins with the opening material in a new key (C at 6:3), so tripartite (1-6:3, 6:3-13:3, 13:3-25) is the alternative; its sections are unequal (5.5, 7, 12 bars). The arrival at 18:1 is not a cadence (diminished seventh to a over C in the bass). About 12 of 25 bars are paradigm members. The piece is made almost entirely of broken chords; z's relation to x (free inversion) is the reader's naming, unsure. The bass at 23:1-24:1 rises chromatically (A F# B G# C A D Bb): worth hearing.
review: Session lead, 12 October: the half cadence at 22:1 checked by hand: the bass leaves D#2 at 21:4 and rests on the beat; the dominant (E major, right hand G#3 B4 G#4 E4) arrives at 22:1 with B3 then E3 in the bass (22:1.25-1.75). Kept as HC; the bass reaches 5 only at 22:1.75.
